question: What protective claim is made about the body such that poison does not enter it even in the case of a bite from great serpents?
premises: A bite from great serpents is possible.
Even if bitten by great serpents, poison does not enter the body.
This is presented as a general claim about that body.
inference: Poison does not enter the body, even if one has been bitten by great serpents.
uncertainties: The basis for this protection is not stated in this verse
plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if bitten by great serpents.
